text: Twelve chambers. That was the easy half. I did not mention there was another half. I am mentioning it now.
Welcome to the second half. I have installed launch pads. They are like stairs, but faster and less forgiving.
There are no white panels in here. Your portal gun is, for once, purely decorative.
Step on the pad with the cube in your hands. It throws whatever is on it. Including you.
You flew a cube across an acid pit. Somewhere, a postal service is weeping with envy.
The exit is on a ledge. The ledge has no stairs. I removed them. They were making things too easy.
The plate up there wants the cube down here. And the sentry up there wants you.
The wall above the ledge is white. Put a portal there, and one down here, and take the cube with you. Then come at the sentry from behind.
You went upstairs without stairs. Your ancestors would be confused, and a little proud.
This pit is longer than the last one. I measured it myself, with a subject.
What goes in fast comes out fast. Where it comes out is up to you.
Fall into a floor portal and leave by one high on the back wall. The higher it is, the further you fly before you land.
You cleared it. I have updated the record, and the subject I measured it with.
The pad throws you at a wall. This is not a mistake. Well. It is not only a mistake.
There is one white panel on this side, and it is very high up. You will be very high up too, briefly.
Put one portal on that high window, and the other one across the pit. Then let the pad throw you into the window.
You turned a wall into a door, in mid air. I have seen worse ideas succeed, but not many.
The receiver is on the ceiling. The laser is on the floor. They have never met. You are going to introduce them.
The door also wants the cube on its plate. It is a door with expensive tastes.
Light goes up out of a floor portal just as happily as it goes sideways. Catch the beam on the pillar, and send it up from right under the target.
You sent light through the floor and into the ceiling. The building is impressed. I am cautiously neutral.
The field runs wall to wall. You can walk through it. The cube cannot. Your portals will not survive it either.
The cube is on the far side. The plate is on this side. You see the difficulty.
Fetch the cube by portal, not on foot. Set the portals up from the far side, shooting back through the field, then carry it through.
The cube went through a wall without touching the field. That is called thinking with doors.
Three lasers, three sentries, one cube. I call it a gauntlet. The sentries call it lunch.
There is a pad. There is always a pad now. I have grown fond of them.
Take the cube onto the pad and you will both fly over the lasers. The sentries guard the door, so do not walk up to them. Arrive behind them instead.
You ran the gauntlet. It ran out of ideas before you did. Do not let it go to your head.
Two pits. One island. One cube, which is on the island, because I put it there.
Get to the island. Then get off the island. In that order, ideally.
A fall from the gantry, out of a portal high on the back wall, lands you on the island. The pad there will do the rest. Take the cube.
Two pits, no swimming. You are becoming difficult to impress, which makes two of us.
The cube is on a shelf you cannot reach. The door wants it on a plate you can. It also wants the laser on its target.
One pair of portals, two jobs. You will have to take turns.
A portal under the cube lets it fall to you. Once it is on the plate, use the portals again for the light: the pillar, then high on the far wall.
You brought the cube down and the light round. Multitasking. I did not know you had it in you.
Three sentries are standing on the only bridge. They are not moving, and neither, for now, are you.
I am told they are very expensive. I am also told they are very heavy.
Open a portal under a sentry and it falls through. Put the other portal somewhere it will not enjoy coming out of. Above the acid, for example.
You threw away three sentries. I will be invoicing you. I will be invoicing you in my head.
This pit is thirty four metres long. Nothing in here can throw you that far. Except gravity, if you let it practise.
There is a floor and a ceiling over here. You may have noticed they line up.
Floor portal, ceiling portal straight above it, and fall. Keep falling. When you are fast enough, move the ceiling portal to the back wall.
Seventy metres a second. You have never been more streamlined. Or more like a projectile.
The final chamber. A pad, a pit, a field, a laser, a cube, two sentries, and a door that wants all of it.
I have prepared a speech for when you finish. I have also prepared one for when you do not. Both are short.
Fly the cube over the pit, take it through the field by portal, put it on the plate. Then catch the light at the pillar and send it up to the target.
Testing is complete. All of it. You may go. I will be here, grading.
